[Guide index](start-here.html) | Guide 4 of 5

This standalone guide uses invented diagnosis records. `icd_flag()` accepts
local data; it neither queries a database nor chooses clinical definitions.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

## 1. Supply the lists you want

```{r data}
library(thipR)
library(dplyr)
records <- data.frame(
  record_id = 1:5, person = c("A", "A", "B", "C", "D"),
  pdx = c(" e11.9 ", "J06", "F20.0", NA, "J06"),
  sdx = c(NA, "F12.1", NA, "", NA)
)
conditions <- list(diabetes = "E11", cannabis = c("F12.1", "F12.2"), psychosis = "F20")
```

Named list elements become output columns. Empty code vectors are allowed and
match no recorded codes. These lists illustrate syntax, not validated phenotypes.

## 2. Flag each record

```{r row-flags}
flags <- icd_flag(
  records, conditions,
  id = "record_id", cols = c("pdx", "sdx"), match = "prefix"
)
records |> left_join(flags, by = "record_id")
```

The result is a separate table: one row per unique ID, with logical condition
columns. Join it explicitly if you want the original fields alongside flags.

## 3. Change the aggregation ID

```{r person-flags}
person_flags <- icd_flag(
  records, conditions,
  id = "person", cols = c("pdx", "sdx"), match = "prefix"
)
person_flags
```

Person A's diagnoses are combined across rows. For entry-window records,
`id = "entry_id"` instead combines diagnoses within each entry. Define the
history/follow-up window **before** flagging; the function does not apply dates.
Do not aggregate by person if separate entry-specific histories are needed.

## 4. Exact versus prefix

```{r exact-prefix}
exact <- icd_flag(records, list(diabetes = "E11"),
                  id = "record_id", cols = "pdx", match = "exact")
prefix <- icd_flag(records, list(diabetes = "E11"),
                   id = "record_id", cols = "pdx", match = "prefix")
data.frame(record_id = exact$record_id, exact = exact$diabetes, prefix = prefix$diabetes)
```

`exact` is the default. `prefix` includes literal subcodes: E11 matches E11.9.
Dots, case and surrounding whitespace are normalized. Prefixes are not regular
expressions; a wildcard or regex is not a substitute for a code list.

### Thai ICD-10-TM codes can have a fifth character

Thai records often add a fifth character for clinical detail, for example
`F10.30` and `F10.31` beneath the four-character `F10.3`. Exact matching on
`F10.3` silently misses those records. A code list built at four-character
resolution, including lists exported from tools that only offer four-character
codes, needs prefix matching to include the more detailed codes:

```{r five-character}
detail <- data.frame(id = 1:3, dx = c("F10.3", "F10.31", "F10.30"))
data.frame(
  id = detail$id, dx = detail$dx,
  exact = icd_flag(detail, list(withdrawal = "F10.3"), "id", "dx", "exact")$withdrawal,
  prefix = icd_flag(detail, list(withdrawal = "F10.3"), "id", "dx", "prefix")$withdrawal
)
```

Before freezing a definition, tabulate which recorded codes, at which lengths
and diagnosis positions, actually occur in your source.

Range notation such as `"Q20-Q26"`, SQL/regex wildcards (`%`, `_`, `?`, `^`,
brackets) and comma- or space-separated lists stop with an error instead of
quietly matching nothing. Write the reviewed codes out explicitly:

```{r explicit-range}
congenital_heart <- paste0("Q", 20:26)  # Q20-Q26, reviewed
congenital_heart
```

`*`, `+` and `/` are kept as literal characters because some sources record
dagger/asterisk or similar notation.

## Missingness and counting

- `TRUE`: at least one selected recorded code matches.
- `FALSE`: there are recorded codes but none match; this is not proof of disease absence.
- `NA`: all selected codes for the ID are blank or missing.

No input row means no output ID; preserve the cohort roster using a left join.
Unknown flags and absent records need an explicit study policy. Flags express
presence, not frequency: requiring two admissions needs a reliable admission key
and an explicit distinct-admission count, not duplicated diagnosis-row counts.

## Filtering versus flagging

`thip_filter_icd()` is a **lazy DB row filter**, with a single code vector and
`cols`. `icd_flag()` is a **local aggregation** for multiple named conditions.
Use standard `collect()` to make the transition explicit. No automatic download
or backend switch occurs. Choose primary versus secondary diagnosis columns
visibly in the call.
